SOCIAL STUDIES — GENERAL ASSESSMENT #5
====

GRADE: Grade 4
SUBJECT: SOCIAL STUDIES
TIME ALLOWED: 45 minutes
TOTAL MARKS: 30
ASSESSMENT: CBC school-based practice paper

INSTRUCTIONS
----
1. Answer all questions.
2. For calculations, show your working and write the units.
3. For multiple choice, choose the one best answer.
4. Check your work before you hand in.

SECTION A — MULTIPLE CHOICE
----
1. Who writes down what is discussed and decided at a meeting? (1 mark)
   A. The secretary
   B. The president
   C. The Speaker
   D. The patron

2. What is a good thing to do at the end of a project? (1 mark)
   A. Throw away records
   B. Blame others
   C. Evaluate what went well and what to improve
   D. Forget about it

3. Who is a leader? (1 mark)
   A. A person who breaks rules
   B. A stranger
   C. A machine
   D. A person who guides and helps others to do something good

4. Which pattern describes each family living far from the next on its own land? (1 mark)
   A. Linear
   B. Clustered
   C. Crowded
   D. Scattered

5. What is child abuse? (1 mark)
   A. Treating a child in a way that harms the child
   B. Teaching a child
   C. Playing with a child
   D. Feeding a child

6. At what age can a Kenyan vote in national elections? (1 mark)
   A. 12 years
   B. 18 years
   C. 10 years
   D. 15 years

7. Which of these actions helps to conserve a historic place? (1 mark)
   A. Leaving litter
   B. Reporting anyone who damages it
   C. Climbing on old walls
   D. Breaking off small pieces

8. Why is it useful to know the size of a county? (1 mark)
   A. It helps with planning services such as roads and clinics
   B. It tells us the price of food
   C. It tells us the weather
   D. It tells us what to eat

9. What is one way factories can protect the environment? (1 mark)
   A. Throw waste into rivers
   B. Burn tyres
   C. Treat waste before releasing it
   D. Cut all trees

10. Which is NOT allowed in Kenyan schools? (1 mark)
   A. Beating pupils
   B. Guiding and counselling pupils
   C. Praising pupils
   D. Talking to pupils

11. What is a clan? (1 mark)
   A. A market
   B. A school
   C. A kind of road
   D. A large family group with a common ancestor

12. Which of these is a way of caring for a river? (1 mark)
   A. Washing cars in it
   B. Planting trees along its banks
   C. Cutting trees at the bank
   D. Throwing rubbish into it

13. Who takes over when the president of the Children's Government is absent? (1 mark)
   A. The visitor
   B. The deputy president
   C. The parent
   D. The cook

14. What is a raw material? (1 mark)
   A. A worker
   B. A material used to make something new
   C. A finished product
   D. A machine

15. What is a duty? (1 mark)
   A. A game
   B. A gift
   C. Something you are expected to do
   D. Something you may not do

SECTION B — STRUCTURED / SHORT ANSWERS
----
16. Give two reasons why we obey school rules. (2 marks)

17. What is a county assembly? (2 marks)

18. Describe the duties of ward and village administrators. (4 marks)

19. Explain why many factories are built near big towns. (3 marks)

20. What is a school motto? (2 marks)

21. Explain what devolution means. (2 marks)
pages.answers:
SOCIAL STUDIES — GENERAL ASSESSMENT #5 · MARKING SCHEME
====

SECTION A
----
1. A — The secretary
   The secretary keeps the minutes.

2. C — Evaluate what went well and what to improve
   Evaluation helps us do better next time.

3. D — A person who guides and helps others to do something good
   Leaders guide and help.

4. D — Scattered
   Scattered means spread widely apart.

5. A — Treating a child in a way that harms the child
   Abuse harms a child's body, feelings or future.

6. B — 18 years
   Adults aged 18 and above can vote.

7. B — Reporting anyone who damages it
   Reporting damage helps protect the place.

8. A — It helps with planning services such as roads and clinics
   Planners need to know how much land there is to cover with services.

9. C — Treat waste before releasing it
   Treating waste avoids pollution.

10. A — Beating pupils
   Teachers are not allowed to beat pupils.

11. D — A large family group with a common ancestor
   A clan traces its origin to one ancestor.

12. B — Planting trees along its banks
   Trees hold the soil and keep the water clean.

13. B — The deputy president
   The deputy helps and takes over.

14. B — A material used to make something new
   Raw materials are used to make products.

15. C — Something you are expected to do
   A duty is a responsibility.

SECTION B
----
16. (2 marks)
   Answer: Rules keep everyone safe and they help everyone to learn.
   Working / marking points: 1 mark for each reason.

17. (2 marks)
   Answer: The county assembly is the group of elected members (MCAs) that makes laws for the county.
   Working / marking points: 1 mark for group of MCAs, 1 mark for making county laws.

18. (4 marks)
   Answer: They bring county services close to people, pass on information, help organise public meetings, and take the community's needs to county leaders.
   Working / marking points: 1 mark for each duty.

19. (3 marks)
   Answer: Many customers live there. Workers live nearby. Roads and other services are available.
   Working / marking points: 1 mark for each reason.

20. (2 marks)
   Answer: A motto is a short sentence that shows what a school stands for or hopes to achieve.
   Working / marking points: 1 mark for short sentence, 1 mark for showing what the school stands for.

21. (2 marks)
   Answer: It means sharing power and resources between the national government and county governments.
   Working / marking points: 1 mark for sharing power, 1 mark for national and county.
